cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Approve the Harmless Version
cards.instruction: Get approval for a harmless version of your plan, then gradually reveal what that approval now commits them to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can my aunt and uncle come for tea? I've put folded towels in the bath like yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tea's fine. My towels are there because the shower leaks, not for guests.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, keeping them handy. Aunt and Uncle can use the towels when they stay tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said tea. And you can't offer them a shower that leaks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll give them your bathroom. You can explain the shower arrangement over the tea you approved.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies towels as guest setup and asks tea permission; A3 masks leak correction while revealing overnight stay; A5 adds a second bathroom without setup.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 tea permission supplies A3 stay claim; B4 unusable shower motivates another bathroom but does not establish one exists.

relationship.evidence: B4 has an immediate practical hosting objection as well as a consent boundary.

heightening.evidence: A5 responsibility for explaining showers would deepen B4 commitment, but the new bathroom is convenient unstated infrastructure.

specificity.evidence: A1 bath towels and B2 leak are intelligible; A5 your bathroom implies a second room without evidence.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 approved tea callbacks are useful, but do not compensate for missing house layout.
